findings.issue: The bond-order ranking rule needs a scope restriction. Higher bond order generally means shorter, stronger bonds when comparing the same bonded elements in comparable environments—not arbitrary bonds. Likewise, a shorter bond is not universally stronger.
findings.evidence: The reference notes that bond length depends on both atomic-core size and bond order, and the worked example compares only carbon–carbon bonds. As standard chemistry beyond the supplied examples, H–H is shorter than N≡N but has a smaller bond energy. Qualify the rule with 'For the same bonded elements in comparable environments, higher bond order generally gives a shorter bond and larger bond energy.' The supplied carbon–carbon values and their ranking are correct.
